notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/3d5f9dd5e70c9da1eb41d6e5b661ec77572fd9d3.png[/img]

Hello everyone!

We’re excited to share a new update that brings several improvements to the game’s interface and overall experience:

[b]Lens Menu Revamp:[/b] The lens menu now features compact icons in the bottom row instead of large text buttons, making it easier to use.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/4493d9a1d78f880da0c331d756abd395d0fdaa2e.png[/img]

[b]Building Menu Clarity[/b]: The number of available slots is now displayed more clearly. Defense lines are shown in a separate list and their descriptions now state that they don’t take up building slots.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/9a90c12cf8b549e7e4a74dd2cc082353e0a3ab59.png[/img]

[b]Resource Unlocks[/b]: Fewer resources are available at the start of the game, helping to declutter the interface and allowing new resource-related elements to unlock gradually.

[b]Top Menu Tooltips[/b]: Tooltips now appear not only when hovering over icons, but also when hovering over text in the top menu.

[b]Slider Improvements[/b]: Sliders now respond to clicks on both the handle and the slider bar itself for smoother interaction.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/7f7681d878b5146bcc677f1c33f052b63e55ffe2.png[/img]

[b]New Secret Promo Codes[/b]: Active Discord users, YouTubers, and community friends can now receive new secret promo codes for signatures!

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]: Fixed an issue where the minus sign was missing in some text elements, resolved lens bugs in the scenario editor, and addressed various other errors.

notes.title: Update you asked for! - v.1.0.2 - Army Movement and UI Overhaul
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/291c02ba73e1045a658714456ce790ee07a5ed77.png[/img]

What’s a good update without listening to the community? We’re back with another round of improvements based on your feedback!

[h3]Interface Improvements
[/h3]

The top bar (income, science, prestige, resources) has been redesigned to take up less space. Resources are now displayed in the same row, without a dropdown menu.

[h3]Army Movement & Pathfinding
[/h3]

Army movement is now more intuitive! The path is dynamically built and shown on the map, not only when holding the right mouse button, but also when hovering after selecting "Move" in the control menu.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/a72bf3c4becd6f783e397a7bae7476fd35f5e696.png[/img]

If you can’t cross a river or sea due to a missing port, an icon and explanation will appear in the province, letting you know why the path is unavailable. This info also appears if your route is longer than expected because you need to go around—so you’ll know where building a port would speed things up.

[h3]Map & Territory Visualization
[/h3]

Country borders are now thicker, making it easier to see where your territory ends.
In lens view mode, your territory is visually distinct from others, so you can quickly tell if those oil deposits are yours or not.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/31682bfe8c5a00d7865b5ced6ee9b7958992a58f.png[/img]

[h3]Country Locator
[/h3]

Clicking your country’s flag or name now highlights your nation’s location on the map and zooms the camera in. Perfect for quickly finding your country—no geography degree required!
Thanks for all your feedback and suggestions. Keep them coming, and enjoy the new update!

Hello! We’re extremely grateful to everyone who sends us feedback about the game—please keep it coming. We read every review and turn them into tasks in our tracker.

[h1]Top Priority – Clarity[/h1]  
Our current top priority is to make the game’s interfaces as clear and user-friendly as possible. After three years of closed beta, we (the developers and veteran players) have grown accustomed to some of the old solutions, which aren’t always obvious to newcomers. That’s definitely on us, so even now, at 2 AM, we’re working on fixes and will keep at it!

Also, starting today, our experienced designer Ivan has joined the team. Early this morning we compiled a list of over 30 tasks—and the first ones are already done. Here’s the new update!

[h1]What’s New in This Update?[/h1]
[list]  
[*] Tutorial hints added: the text now contains hyperlinks that, when clicked, instantly show the relevant city or country on the game map.  
[*] Hovering over the “Relations” icon now displays which factors contribute to the final score.  
[*] In the “Lenses” and “Buildings” menus, we’ve added tooltips with all the info you need to decide.  
[/list]

We’ve reduced the size of text and UI elements in various game windows so that large monitors have more free space for the map.

notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/16a01f49f38eb2096cca9b3bd18316dac42a91ae.png[/img]

Hey rulers!

This update is particularly exciting, as we've improved detalization of the map, as part of the ongoing process of making the game look nicer! To quote a friend of ours, "I'm seeing a 2D Risk-like game turning into Europa Universalis, and that's mindblowing". And while we wouldn't dream of competing with the titans in the genre, the game does look nicer this way, don't you agree?

[i][b]Please note:[/b] Most of the new features are available in the demo, but you can gain access to unlimited games in Warnament's closed beta for as much as $0.99! It includes a multiplayer mode, a full technology tree, 3 more political institutions, a scenario editor & a standalone map editor app.

Head over to our [url=https://ludenio.itch.io/warnament]itch.io page[/url] or straight to [url=https://warnament.com]warnament.com[/url] to start playing in a few clicks![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/3d960f7d35693070f652030904d4820cb8409bb2.png[/img]
[previewyoutube=Jv4M9OiCUMM;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3][h3]v0.9.34 Released![/h3][/h3]
[list]
[*] Added different types of terrain (they depend on a province's relief and level of economic development). If you zoom in the camera, you can see the textures and also hear ambient sounds. For example, a province with a high level of infrastructure will have city sounds, while in a desert you'll mostly hear wind
[*] Currently, terrain types like mountains, deserts, and cold regions do not provide any bonuses and are not set by default on standard maps, but this will be addressed in future updates
[*] You can now enable or disable clouds in the settings (they are disabled by default on mobile devices)
[*] In the scenario editor, you can now check whether countries are neighbors when creating an event
[*] Flags have been added to the Declare War menu
[*] Fixed the placement of ships received through events (previously they spawned randomly; now they spawn near a shipyard or, if that's not available, in the sea or a river. Previously, they could even spawn in a lake)

notes.title: Glorious Evolution - Warnament Dev Update #15
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/1b5c9703da11e736136353a165601917adea61ae.png[/img]

Hey, rulers!

What a time to be alive, huh? Wherever you live, you probably noticed that the news headlines seem to get crazier by the day: we're even guessing how long it will take before they become undistinguishable from our [url=https://www.youtube.com/@warnament/videos]YouTube videos[/url]’ headlines. In any case, as we believe that violence should stay in video games, we keep making Warnament, not war.

[h3]A Year at War(nament)[/h3]

The name ‘Glorious Evolution’ was chosen for this piece for a reason: little by little, we found ourselves with quite a different game by the end of the year. Here's a very brief list of the biggest changes we made in the past 12 months:
[list]
[*] Completely reworked map visuals
[*] New interface
[*] Win/lose conditions for the game
[*] Reworked economy
[*] A bunch of new visual effects, sounds and music
[*] A whole galaxy of new gameplay mechanics for war & peace
[/list]
And of course, there was the glorious [url=https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ludenio.a7]Warnament release on Google Play[/url]! Although it still is an early access version, you can try it for free, if a you own one of the (thousands of) supported devices.

Effectively, this creates a situation in which Warnament is simultaneously available in 3 forms (almost like an anime character, or maybe a boss from a soulslike game!). Let's review them real quick:

[b]Steam:[/b] currently, only the demo is available here, but this will be the main platform for us for Early Access on PC, so make sure you add Warnament to your wishlist to get notified when it happens. The demo is updated as often as other versions, but has limited content.

[b]Itch.io:[/b] there's a demo that you can [url=https://ludenio.itch.io/warnament]launch in your browser[/url], and you can also get access to the closed beta for a small fee (starting at $0.99). It's playable on PC, Mac and Linux, it has full content, and comes with the standalone map editor.

[b]Android:[/b] has pretty much the same content as the closed beta, but is only playable on Android devices (duh). It's free to play, with an option to buy cosmetic stuff. And there's no map editor on Android.

At some point in the future all these platforms will be synced with each other in terms of gameplay features (pretty much like a giant robot assembles from smaller robots in anime!). We'll be in touch when this day arrives. As for now, let's talk about the most recent improvements of Warnament.

Getting back to the Android version: it has badges now! Fancy little ribbons that are given out for committing certain actions (like wishlisting the game on Steam), winning in community tournaments, and being an admin on [url=https://discord.gg/WwfsH8mnuz]Warnament's Discord Server[/url]. Unlocking the cosmetics also grants a special badge:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/6a04241f04e050f518d8690381ef35ba766a205f.png[/img]

One day those pretty things will appear on Steam too, don't you worry!

As for more meaningful and gameplay-related features, the province menu has gone through a massive upgrade. Now you can view the economy, population, and amount of money per turn of any country on the map (e.g. you can check the population of the enemy's province and think a hundred times whether it's worth attacking the enemy):

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/4fe6eb13ab7959ade465c364c5e6dd156cb9e91f.jpg[/img]

From the same menu, you can see information about the whole country, including those that you do not rule yet - given that you are not in war with, nor under sanctions of that country:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/d6f0054d18334795f8676c48af51cd9257ecf445.png[/img]

The provinces are now playing a much bigger role in the game: whether it's a small town or a big city will influence your economy and the production in an individual provice itself. For one, factories perform better, when built in cities, so mind that when planning your budget.

Next thing that was massively improved is multiplayer. Most changes happened under the cape, but you will definitely notice them, if you play online frequently.

[list]
[*] Servers started from singleplayer mode are now much more stable (that part of code was written from scratch)
[*] You can now create multiplayer sessions on custom maps
[*] Added spectator mode to the game
[*] Added an option to select a country when connecting to a server. You can pick any country that is not yet taken by another player
[*] Next features that we're planning to add include teamplay mode and an in-game event schedule
[*]
[/list]
If you prefer a more hand-tailored gameplay instead (or in addition to) the joy of collective online madness, we've added an option to create events in user-made scenarios. With the latest update, you can make bots encounter these events as well:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/80ac73b1583f79e804e1e389754c37cdd694be09.png[/img]

But whatever's your preferred way to conquer the world, there's now an option to review your glorious deeds once it's over: we have finally added timelapse mode to the game, and it looks mesmerizing:

[previewyoutube=U3YW5s6fubc;full][/previewyoutube]

Oh, and here's the latest gameplay video from our channel, in case you missed it:

[previewyoutube=tSudDZU4EGc;full][/previewyoutube]

The next big feature we're working on will probably become a great source material for timelapses: we're planning to add historical mode to the game, in which the events will be synced with the main dates from the history books. Have fun messing up the past! We'll introduce it in one of the next updates.

Until we meet again!

notes.title: We tried to make a trailer with AI. Oh boy... - Warnament Dev Update #14
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/483d59fbba0e5749b7bd1d14b31e26fe651fee27.png[/img]

Hey rulers!

It’s been an intense month, to say the least, as we have been pushing hard to [url=https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ludenio.a7&hl=en]release Warnament on Android[/url]! If you wish to play the game right now, don’t hold yourself back. It’s free to play with an option to support us by buying cosmetic items.

But today, we’ll be telling a different story. Warnament is released in beta mode on Google Play (which means you won’t be seeing user reviews, but we will). Our primary focus is still to hit Early Access on Steam, but the release is a release, so we decided it deserves a proper trailer.

Since at Luden.io, we’re big fans of experimenting, so we ended up having to answer a question: are AI algorithms of today good enough to generate animations for trailers? The answer is… errrr… Well, more on that below.

[previewyoutube=2_63DDvFa7k;full][/previewyoutube]

We cooperated with [b]Lev Koretski[/b], a video maker whose works you might’ve seen on Steam pages of Black Skylands, Graveyard Keeper, Cartel Tycoon, and other renowned games. You should definitely check out his [url=https://youtu.be/tptBWDN5lgQ?si=0SHRwlD6vWoUyTt0]sample reel[/url], especially if you’re an indie game maker!

Since Warnament only has a tiny dev team, we wouldn’t be able to afford fancy animations and visual effects. Therefore, we decided to refer to the silicon wisdom of AI models for animation. Long story short: it was not as easy as we estimated, and only tiny bits of what was generated by the model made their way to the trailer.

A quote from Lev himself and some goofy tryouts is below:

[quote][Working with AI models] became not so much a help but rather a perpetually breaking crutch that we still had to learn to work with.

Along the way, I encountered numerous difficulties. I tried many neural networks available for free (such as Runway, Vidu, Google Veo, Dream Machine by Luma), and all of them operated more or less the same way: you upload 1-2 pictures, and the AI creates animation.

You can write a prompt, but often it doesn't work. Or, you need to go through a bunch of formulations to get the desired result. It feels like the developers of neural networks deliberately limit creators with prompts so that as many attempts are made as possible and the [number of props provided per month in a] subscription runs out.[/quote]

Here’s a bunch of things we got in response to our prompts. Check out this nightmare fuel (prompt - [b]“finger presses the red button”[/b]):

[previewyoutube=7sp80XZnjYA;full][/previewyoutube]

Animating machines worked fairly ok, unless they had rotating elements, such as wheels or propellers, in which case things tended to turn out… not so well (prompt: [b]“Panoramic camera movement, left to right, planes flies shooting at the houses, fire below“[/b]):

[previewyoutube=ljBHUbdJT8E;full][/previewyoutube]

And how do you like those people morphing into artillery? This takes the concept of giving one’s life for their country to a whole new level:

[previewyoutube=l-xoNsWiGKM;full][/previewyoutube]

And here’s the Eiffel Tower merging with a house (prompt: [b]“slow approach to a nuclear explosion”[/b]):

[previewyoutube=1fsGv37oAbY;full][/previewyoutube]

Can you spot that one soldier who’s running backwards?

[previewyoutube=94XApeZxFc4;full][/previewyoutube]

Some more creepy hands to top all that (prompts: [b]“finger presses the red button”, “flags fluttering in the background”[/b]):

[previewyoutube=9HGWhF9WtX0;full][/previewyoutube]

[previewyoutube=5q95XJlJgvU;full][/previewyoutube]

To be fair, just a couple of years back AI models were drawing creepy pictures, but a lot of progress was made in this field since. So chances are good that one day they will become a trustworthy video maker’s helper. This day just has not yet come.

As for the trailer - let us know how you like it! And if you want to discuss anything Warnament-related with us directly (or just exchange some memes), come by our [url=https://discord.com/invite/WwfsH8mnuz]Discord server[/url].

Just a reminder in case you skipped it: [url=https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ludenio.a7&hl=en]Warnament is now available to play for free on Google Play[/url]! Next time, we’ll tell a couple of stories about how we were preparing for the release.

Until we meet again!

notes.title: The State of War - Warnament Dev Update #13
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/c380e51300960fadc4cfdbf829db1d527853297b.png[/img]

Hey, rulers!

It's been a while since we reported on Warnament's progress. It's partly because we got carried away with developing the game. Time passed by as we introduced small changes to the game every two weeks. A couple of new political institutions here, a nice vignette for the map there, a bunch of fixes on the server side over here… Little by little, we ended up with quite a different game: more stable, more pretty, and with much deeper gameplay.

In this dev update, we will try to review the most significant additions to Warnament. We still keep to our philosophy of the game being compact and easy to start playing, but more experienced rulers will find themselves with a much bigger toolkit for dominating the world.

Even the gloriest of wars must come to an end at some point (which is a good thing, we might add), and so does Warnament. There's now a limit of 100 turns per session (or 2 hours in multiplayer, by default), after which the countries are rated by their success in controlling territory, the state of economics, and the number of vassal states.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/7900f142b5dd5714f953b4197fff7d4153b54e30.png[/img]

A nice place to try out this new system is our new scenario - World War II - in which history may take some unexpected terms: from the secession of Catalonia to the re-establishment of the Russian Empire. This scenario relies heavily on the new rebellion mechanics: if there's too much discontent among the population, you might end up with some of your provinces declaring independence. It's also how Israel might appear on the map in a quite different way than it did, according to history books.

If (or should we say - when?) it comes to war, rulers of Warnament will have more instruments at their disposal - both military and diplomatic. The former includes garrisons, the size of which depends on the overall economic situation in a province. From now on, one just can't move an army to another country's province and claim it as their own - they would have to completely destroy the garrison.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/d1ec32aa2a9e0e81ca63b207c5e9957026d8041c.jpg[/img]

s for battles, there's now an element of randomness: even if you attack with a bigger army, there's still a chance of losing a battle.

And when the fog of war dissipates and the negotiations for peace are happening, one of the conditions of the treaty may be creating a demilitarized zone in the bordering provinces. No armies can be present in such provinces for a selected amount of turns.

Some peculiar changes were made in domestic politics, especially for those preferring a more… extravagant style of play. Communist countries might treat their population with good old repressions, which may cause paranoia among the authorities, resulting in deteriorated relations with other countries. Which is probably bad news for them, because communist states now have a perk of increased artillery range.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/eb4662c3b8c9d99470928c831b2f7abff07b0637.png[/img]

Fascist states have a whole new array of options for going wild, and establishing policies of xenophobia and/or occultism: if you ever considered devoting your life to serving the dark gods - that's your chance (we don't judge). Monarchs in Warnament now have more options, too: if you think that the progress has gone too far, you can always return to feudalism or re-establish serfdom. You are the king, after all!

Regardless of your political regime, the new, more flexible, and deep economic system in Warnament will be at your disposal. You can now allocate a budget for each province individually, which influences its garrison size and the number of slots available for buildings. And on the national level, you can financially stimulate science, infrastructure, or population independently, allowing you to fine-tune the economics to match your style of play.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/d6f16acec5ecddf274f3e5f4d4bf23d4ccf7d36a.png[/img]

These are the most prominent changes in the gameplay, but any game is more than just mechanics: other aspects of Warnament were improved as well. We've worked a lot on the server side of the game, and now any player can start hosting a multiplayer session at any time.

We've also made quite a few changes to the game's UI and UX and added pretty borders for countries on the map:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/5e96bab1309f7e7883d839a11b686dfe41b7fd59.jpg[/img]

Last but not least, we added sounds and several new music tracks to the game! You can check them out in one of our gameplay videos (which we're posting on our [url=https://www.youtube.com/@warnament]YouTube channel[/url] every week):

[previewyoutube=ULSNEyba0AU;full][/previewyoutube]

As for our plans for the near future - we've got a surprise for you: we're now preparing Warnament to be released on Android. No date is nailed to the wall yet, but our expectations are to ship the game by the end of September. Warnament will be released as a free-to-play game with an option to buy cosmetic items for money.

On one hand, this is an intermediate stage of the game's development: our main focus is to hit Early Access on Steam. But, on the other hand, we already have an experience of releasing a mobile grand strategy: [url=https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.DenisMakhortov.ColdPath&hl=en_US]Cold Path[/url], Warnament's spiritual precessor, was initially released on Android and accumulated a handsome number of 1+ million downloads. So if you enjoy mobile gaming, make sure to [url=https://discord.gg/WwfsH8mnuz]join our Discord server[/url] to be among the first to know about the upcoming release.

A friendly reminder: if you prefer playing Warnament on your PC, there's a [url=https://warnament.com]closed beta[/url] which costs as little as $0.99 to start playing.

That's it for today, rulers! We'll keep you posted on Warnament's progress. Until we meet again!

notes.title: Why maps matter, and how they work? - Warnament Dev Update #12
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/a591e09beb8199f463b1ad28c056be64d7a47f8d.png[/img]

[i][b]To read all Warnament's dev logs, subscribe to our [url=https://warnament.substack.com]official newsletter[/url][/b][/i]

Hey everyone! The first question from the title is easy to answer: Warnament is a grand strategy game, which means that players spend most of the time looking at the map. So it not only has to be pretty but also easy to design and fun to interact with.

Today we'll talk about how maps are structured in Warnament, but first here's a quick summary of what the heck is going on - for our new readers.

[h2]The Most Important Things About Warnament[/h2]

[b]When's the release?[/b] We're aiming to go into Early Access in 2024

[b]What happens now?[/b] You can play Warnament's [url=https://warnament.com]closed beta[/url] for as much as $0.99. It is updated bi-monthly, and includes map editor & multiplayer mode, along with the access to the devs’ eyes & ears

[b]And what if I don't?[/b] There's also a free demo here on Steam. It doesn't have all the features but also gets regular updates, including some new content. And don't forget to add Warnament to your wishlist, so you get notified when it is released:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1201700/Warnament/

With that aside, let's get back to maps in Warnament.

[h3]Map Editor Begins[/h3]
To anticipate the importance of the map editor, keep in mind that we started working on it before Warnament was contemplated: we knew we'd start working on a new strategy game eventually, which implies having an editor from the start.

We wanted to make it easy to handle, but also responsive to a designer's actions. Unlike heavyweight grand strategies like Hearts of Iron, there are no rivers, height differences, or terrain types. But at the same time, the editor allows much flexibility when it comes to provinces and their borders.

[h3]How maps work in Warnament[/h3]
In Warnament, each map contains provinces, and each province is a polygon with multiple vertices. You can scale and move vertices, as seen in real-life industrial map-drawing tools, which allows you to shape the provinces on your map any way you like.

Sometimes it's more than one polygon per province - in case you want to create an enclave outside of a country's main territory, which is very easy in Warnament's map editor.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/1819683125663472664ee3e3b401cbbe4755b068.png[/img]

When you're done marking borders, click the ‘Export’ button - and the map is ready to be loaded in the game. At this point, it is not yet fully playable (though you're welcome to try) - it needs a scenario, in which you will also set colors for all the participating countries, among other things.

The map editor was designed in a way to be as much friendly to player-generated content as possible, so handling custom maps is very easy. You can just copy the .map file in Warnament folder, and see it in the list of other maps when you launch the game.

Each map file also contains data of each pixel on the screen corresponding to a certain province, which decreases response time upon clicking a great deal.

Combined together, the scenario editor and map editor provide tools for creating beautiful things:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/91c2f52e01c2d15d250b6282a84fd3723c73101f.png[/img]

And a little bit odd but still beautiful things:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/1240165306f2fb4fe73172f7baa0c912a9350951.png[/img]

Maybe even a tiger, why not:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/0667b009d355ad7dc88b35e04b1bf7dcf6573643.png[/img]

[h3]The final touch[/h3]
But before a map is loaded, a few things will happen to make it shine!

Each map consists of three layers: polygons, inland effect texture, and coast effect texture. Here they are, taken apart for this picture:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/c4500d8939394ddbd7dc9aac9f6764a08f81f4b2.png[/img]

And here they are, united for the greater purpose (serving as playground for your geopolitical experiments):

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/6827675a937095c91ec25e24f4dfdc3991d87221.png[/img]

notes.title: Rebellion With a Cause - Warnament Dev Update #11
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/888ec07c95c57aad6fdb5be233ddef068a9ec163.png[/img]

[i][b]To read all Warnament's dev logs, subscribe to our [url=https://warnament.substack.com]official newsletter[/url][/b][/i]

[h2]The Most Important Things About Warnament[/h2]

[b]When's the release?[/b] We're aiming to go into Early Access by the beginning of 2024

[b]What happens now?[/b] You can play Warnament's [url=https://warnament.com]closed beta[/url] for as much as $0.99. It is updated bi-monthly, and includes map editor & multiplayer mode, along with the access to the devs’ eyes & ears

[b]And what if I don't?[/b] There's also a free demo here on Steam. It doesn't have all the features but also gets regular updates, including some new content:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1201700/Warnament/

With that aside, let's finally talk about what's new in Warnament!

[previewyoutube=miMvb-Zqrf8;full][/previewyoutube]

We know it's been a while since our last Dev Update, but the changes we bring you this time are, quite literally, revolutionary!

That is: a couple of weeks back we introduced strikes and rebellions, subsequently followed by good old separatism. Typically, things start brewing if you raise the taxes too high. Lowering them is an intuitive solution, but if that doesn't help, there are a bunch of political decisions for you to make and cool down the troublemakers. A couple of especially interesting decisions will be introduced for Fascism real soon (consider it a teaser).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/4deb156dd6d889020fb5698b711c497a15e0f4d7.png[/img]

Reacting to events can also influence the overall level of discontent in your domain, so answer wisely!

Remember: being left without attention, strikes may turn into full-swing separatist movements. In this case, you'll have to decide whether to let your rebellious provinces declare independence or to go to war with them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/2daec187ecb2bf4912ac3d8851fb0051c0248c88.png[/img]

But hey: if your people rise against you, at least you can crush them in style! Our great interface renovation goes on, and will keep us occupied at least until the end of the year. This time we've dramatically improved the window with overall country stats:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/7ffff95d88383c3c37f79d77ab5fc70d4a358e04.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/016462aa6a85f0c9591fa4567bc7a5a4792f6631.png[/img]

Also, the menu of Political Institutions was brought into correspondence with current UI/UX style. It has pretty pictures, too:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/3bb7b42b2e5846f0096641ad51b783c1430b3e7d.png[/img]

If you're participating in out [url=https://warnament.com]closed beta[/url], you probably noticed a bunch of important improvements in the map editor. notes.title: Completely Reformed - Warnament Dev Update #10
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/cb6d06225aa28d183d8a4e4084de4561eedf55e6.png[/img]

[i][b]To read all Warnament's dev logs, subscribe to our [url=https://warnament.substack.com]official newsletter[/url][/b][/i]

[h2]The Most Important Things About Warnament[/h2]

[b]When's the release?[/b] We're aiming to go into Early Access by the beginning of 2024

[b]What happens now?[/b] You can play Warnament's [url=https://warnament.com]closed beta[/url] for as much as $0.99. It is updated bi-monthly, and includes map editor & multiplayer mode, along with the access to the devs’ eyes & ears

[b]And what if I don't?[/b] There's also a free demo here on Steam. It doesn't have all the features but also gets regular updates, including some new content:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1201700/Warnament/

With that aside, let's finally talk about what's new in Warnament!

[previewyoutube=nqC_hIsLG68;full][/previewyoutube]

Oh, what's this video all about? It's just another update on [url=https://www.youtube.com/@warnament]Warnament YouTube channel[/url], which you're totally welcome to subscribe to! There's a new video every week, so come by to find yourself in the thick of the development process!

If you're not a video watching type, here's a short summary! We've got an interesting update for the scenario editor: it now allows you to create custom reforms! A ‘reform’ in Warnament is an event when a country evolves like a pokémon, and becomes something completely different. Like that time France became the French Empire or when some folks established the United States of Europe. Well, now you can create these events on your own!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/07c21936003b16cb663a127362c5442dfca9c848.png[/img]

You can create up to 6 reform for each country, which is convenient because there're 6 political regimes in the game, and you can create an option for one of each.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/501c3e70f19b779b42d7e8344c57bef188a5d085.png[/img]

The latter is completely optional though. For example, on these screenshots you can see the Benelux Federation, which can be formed under any political regime. It does, however, have other condition: to be able to call oneself Benelux Federation, one must control the land of BElgium, NEtherlands, and LUXembourg simulatneously. Because otherwise it would be awkward.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/4c3fca460db9488756248dd9d400ab5988073160.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/6e3cd5b8df088c17a1b9bc81f51785d1712de70a.png[/img]

And check out our new interface! The main game screen was completely reformed, which was totally worth it, because you, the players, will be spending 90% of your game time here!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/99f35693d8129a78562806c404748cb389909337.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/b8a233c6eda1f404f468367f75eda1218f9c3246.png[/img]

The game looks more consistent now, which shows in (seemingly) small details, too: we have created a special palette for the game map, to avoid random/weird color combinations:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/f009337581d3661d727d72cf1992d47eaa396025.png[/img]

Getting to gameplay changes, bots can now issue ultimatums to you, demanding to stop aggression towards a country or to decrease the amount of your troops, if bots consider it too big.

If you do not comply within a certain number of turns, get ready for war:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/e7b95a611424e4bc3b18ba46918b1d3f098719eb.png[/img]

Warnament is a rather easy to learn kind of game in the given genre, but now we leave no chance to not understand its rules: there's now a tutorial campaign that activates upon first launch of the game. 

You will have some fun suppressing communist uprisings in Weimar Germany, returning control over the land temporarily known as the Free State of Bottleneck - and learning how to recruit troops, control your armies, and produce artillery on the way!

[h3]Up Next[/h3]

Now that the new palette is ready, we need to introduce it to the existing maps. Existing reforms must be implemented into the new system, and new reforms will be added as well. The plan is to make it so every country has multiple reforms to choose from, which will hopefully increase replayability.

We will also keep improving scenario and the map editors in the upcoming week. User-generated content is the fuel of Warnament, and we're so very grateful to our awesome community maps and scenario creators for the awesome job the are doing to entertain fellow players! By the way, if you're not on our Discord server yet, you're [url=https://discord.com/invite/27VPCABcRg]welcome to join at any time[/url].

See you in a month, with more exciting Warnament-related news!

notes.title: Of AIs and UIs - Warnament Dev Update #9
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/6495ab1fcbec15b80406e038a8262583732605af.png[/img]

[i][b]To read all Warnament's dev logs, subscribe to our [url=https://warnament.substack.com]official newsletter[/url][/b][/i]

[h2]The Most Important Things About Warnament[/h2]

[b]When's the release?[/b] We're aiming to go into Early Access by the beginning of 2024

[b]What happens now?[/b] You can play Warnament's [url=https://warnament.com]closed beta[/url] for as much as $0.99. It is updated bi-monthly, and includes map editor & multiplayer mode, along with the access to the devs’ eyes & ears

[b]And what if I don't?[/b] There's also a free demo here on Steam. It doesn't have all the features but also gets regular updates, including some new content:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1201700/Warnament/

With that aside, let's finally talk about what's new in Warnament!

[h2](Inter)Face Off[/h2]
Some heroes do not wear capes. When a game has a great UI, nobody really notices it. But when it's janky & clumsy - it will haunt your players no matter how engaging the gameplay is.

Apparently, this was Warnament's case. We decided to solve this problem like big boys: we called a professional designer lady to make things look smart.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/36350f2b58d10409e2c13802925cc075b88f74eb.png[/img]

There was a lot of very professional communication when we were discussing prototypes, moving objects around in Figma, and incorporating cutting-edge usability ideas into our game. This process is far from being finished - it took us about a month to make the main menu look shiny. But the results are starting to show already:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/4c6880707397c4bafbb426ddb3d658161b62d45b.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/c54bdb9753eee95f1eb44dd57aa595a1d7616715.png[/img]

Oh, and while she was at it, Julia the UI/UX designer suggested a new version of Warnament's logo as well. Here's some more ‘old vs. new’ content:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/945492fa271750235fa37ad2eaf86a36e0f54fc7.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/fcbdf2821e515e50be6e89fe9afd57b1ee831ac1.png[/img]

Which one do you like more? You're very welcome to [url=https://discord.gg/QQfV2pXxwB]join our Discord[/url] server, and discuss it with us in person!

Next step would be, of course integrating this style into the rest of the game. And while we were at it, we made new covers for these humble developer updates, and for our YouTube videos, too (don't forget to [url=https://www.youtube.com/@warnament]subscribe[/url], if you haven't already):

[previewyoutube=hyy8pviHk8g;full][/previewyoutube]

And while menus, windows, and video covers were being taken care of by a pro, we could concentrate on making Warnament's gameplay more complex! And that’s exactly what we were up to.

[h2]Event Management
[/h2]

In Warnament, there are six ideological institutions to choose from, and now that choice matters even more - and choices that your opponents (human or AI) make will influence your experience, too! We have introduced a wide array (6 per each political institution) of new random events, that are specific to the regimes in power in neighboring countries.

For example, one of your citizens might start a political scandal by participating in an anti-government rally in a Democratic country next door. Or one of your Communist neighbors might decide to nationalize all business enterprises in their country - including those owned by your citizens. In any case, you get to deal with the consequences.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/e3f7f6e6a4d870978050aeabdd3d1e41112bf7f7.png[/img]

These events may turn out quite well for you, bringing additional Prestige points, but choose carefully because it's also very possible to ruin your relationship with a neighbor and find yourself in a state of warfare.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/93d55fe51ce73a1c64cd18af0f4dda62c710ca91.png[/img]

[h2]Can a Robot Write a Symphony (of War)?[/h2]

In 2023, it is not uncommon for a human being to be negotiating with an artificial mind. We couldn't stand aside, and now you will have to deal with way more sophisticated computer opponents.

From now on, bots rely heavily on relationships with you and other countries, when making decisions. If you're on good terms with someone, they will be more likely to agree to your conditions when negotiating. And vice versa: what started as a petty squabble, might turn into a holocaust.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/50c5e36d814cecb78e702000eac9e6206e540677.png[/img]

There are many factors that influence your relationships with other countries. Some of them cannot be easily changed: for example, if someone's in conflict with your country's ideology. But if you've got some Prestige points to spend, you can refer to the new feature, allowing your diplomats to oil the wheels of international affairs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/cd026af3abe0f5e2859ee7bc18fc696c7c3348e0.png[/img]

By the way, sometimes being enemies with someone might be a good thing, too: you see, AI opponents don't like it when a country attacks another country, so declaring a war results in a strong relationship penalty. So you might try and provoke someone (like, by using good old insults - as seen in real life) to start shooting at your troops, so you could convince other rulers to fight on your side.

[h2]Up Next[/h2]

Next month we will continue adding more depth to the gameplay: for example, by adding mini-goals to motivate the players, especially in the early stages of the game. Another thing we're working on is ultimatums: an option to demand something from another country and automatically start a war if the conditions are not met in a timely manner.

And here's a little bonus for those of you who would like a more in-depth look at game development: Oleg Chumakov, head of Luden.io, wrote an [url=https://defold.com/2023/09/07/Defold-x-Luden-io/]article for Defold official blog[/url], in which he's talking about our studio's experience with this very interesting engine. There's [url=https://defold.com/2023/09/07/Defold-x-Luden-io/#warnament]part about Warnament[/url], too!

See you in a month, with more exciting Warnament-related news!

notes.title: Warnament Dev Update #8: The Game is On!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/de730f422f94658b620be113e9cd630dad546187.png[/img]

[i][b]To read all Warnament's dev logs, subscribe to our [url=https://warnament.substack.com]official newsletter[/url][/b][/i]

[h2]The Most Important Things About Warnament[/h2]

[b]When's the release?[/b] We're aiming to go into Early Access by the beginning of 2024

[b]What happens now?[/b] You can play Warnament's [url=https://warnament.com]closed beta[/url] for as much as $0.99. It is updated bi-monthly, and includes map editor & multiplayer mode, along with the access to the devs’ eyes & ears

[b]And what if I don't?[/b] There's also a free demo here on Steam. It doesn't have all the features but also gets regular updates, including some new content:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1201700/Warnament/

With that aside, let's finally talk about what's new in Warnament!

[h2]New Diplomatic Tools: Trading And Making Friends[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/c6a80498085d2216afb5d465b3ee473e2af7fb91.png[/img]

You can now exchange goods, machinery, and even entire provinces with other countries. Needless to say, that adds a new level of depth: if you happen to be a small contry but a filthy rich one, you can become a major player on the global politics arena.

Of course, if a country applied sanctions on you, they won't deal with you. If you have a beef with one of your neighbours, it will also make trading difficult, at the very least. But since the last update you can use finesse and start gradually improving your relationships with other countries with the means of diplomacy. Gameplay-wise it means spending some prestige points, so make sure you have plenty.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/42b156ebcb411a91ce8ec43420fd05b387c27ae3.png[/img]

Last but not least, you will now be recieving answers to your proposals instantly, without having to wait for the next term. It works in the multiplayer, too: the other player will see your offer and be able to answer it immediately. But thread lightly, because that means wars can be declared instantly, too. So make sure you have your troops ready in case things go south.

[h2]Shock & A…rtillery[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/3a08e8cd65fcbd691699720e2fe4babd16ad8fe4.png[/img]

Speaking of troops, we've got a couple of newcomers! Enter Shock Troops: they're like your regular infantry but stronger and resistant to chemical warfare. To convert regular troops to these elite swashbucklers, you'll have to construct a new building called Training Camp.

[previewyoutube=3dRN2CvRbgo;full][/previewyoutube]

Our other fighter is the almighty Artillery: it can strike your enemies from afar but there's a payoff - cannons do not have much durability and are therefore vulnerable to all kinds of attacks. Artillery comes with it's own new building, too: the Machine Factory.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/3705f2c192e2daa3a93e1624d8ac7f076cb2d75a.gif[/img]

Oh, and don't forget: with these guys around, Steel becomes one of the most precious resources out there. Need to improve a building? Steel. Build a fleet? Steel! Artillery, tanks, training Shock Infantry? It's steel, still. Steel!

[h2]Technical Improvements: Better, Faster, Stronger[/h2]

In multiplayer, the players are now receiving not only scenario data from the server but the map data, too. That means, if you run a server, you're free to upload any map to it, and any player will be able to join a session, regardless of whether they have this map or not!

We also made a bunch of smaller but still very important improvements regarding map loading speed optimization, and the map editor. Might not sound so epic but our players are loving it:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/0ef4daa2aac8decb7b3e786d863a55fe7767ea5c.jpg[/img]

Speaking of the players: if you want more content for Warnament (scenarios, maps etc.) then our [url=https://discord.gg/QQfV2pXxwB]Discord server[/url] is the place to go. We have a frightfully active community of awesome players over there.

[h2]Up Next: Of AI's and UI's[/h2]

In the next couple of weeks we will be working of completely redesigning the game interface: we're consulting with a dedicated UI/UX designer, so it's serious business, folks! Real deal.

After that, bots will get their own reboot. We'll teach them to create their own game events, so they could decide to help you in a war (if they like you enough), or insult and attack you (if they don't).

Warnament is coming into its full glory with every update, so bear with us: good times are ahead!

notes.title: Warnament Dev Update #7: A Demo to Remember
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/650f93a17726561bfad808519879abe9e9e013c8.png[/img]

[b][i]To read all Warnament's dev logs, subscribe to our [url=https://warnament.substack.com]official newsletter [/url][/i][/b]

Hey everyone! Welcome to Warnament Dev Updates! Warnament is a grand strategy game, made by a solo dev Denis Makhortov. It is as deep as classic games in the genre, but only takes minutes to get into action. You can play out historic scenarios or create your own: take control of a nation on a global map and take it to glory by taking over territories and achieving military, technical, cultural, or political advantage. It is a spiritual successor to Cold Path, another game with a similar philosophy.

[i]Written by: Denis Makhortov / Editor: Georgii Kurgan[/i]

[previewyoutube=eWN91RfbJxU;full][/previewyoutube]

Do you know there's a [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1201700/Warnament]Warnament Demo on Steam[/url] now? Have you played our demo? Seriously, we think it'd be mighty fine if you played our demo, and then play it some more. We got Luxembourg, remember?

Okay, we didn't want to come off as pushy, but we hope you can understand: you (normally) only release a demo once, so it's hard for us to think/talk about anything else. So we're gonna talk about how we are improving the demo, so you could play a better demo!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/7e035440be53c5520d703d87eea579861d594ddc.jpg[/img]

As you might know, there's also a  [url=https://warnament.com][b]closed beta[/b][/url] (which you can totally become a part of) happening alongside with the demo. It's particularly cool because it gives a dev a lot of feedback to improve the game upon. One of the little tweaks we introduced is that now you must have an excel of at least 400 troops (or 1 tank) to annex a province. So if there's a unit of 9000 enemy troops in the area, you'd need over 9000 soldiers of your own, 9400+, to be precise.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/c1aac0c5b590c87d262759cfe55a562450e14695.jpg[/img]

But there's good news, too! Chemical weaponry has been reinforced and now destroys up to 40% of enemy's infantry: the exact number depends on whether there's a Fortress in the province and the type of landscape:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/a5f345a08ebca1cc95831c5021bb7f062dda5be6.jpg[/img]

Or you can just include the mass production of tanks into your country's political philosophy. Because seriously, why select Totalitarism of Revanchism when you can get yourself an army of roaring death machines:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/e329bca30b07d678a4de4f39e164b510461d4ecb.jpg[/img]

Some work has been done over the Technology Tree, too. Naturally, we've had to cut off some not-so-polished features for the demo, leaving only those we were sure about:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/7c29cc0c213a218a144d42ddbba66116ef24bb0e.jpg[/img]

We'd like our demo players to really feel comfortable, so we continue working on the interface of the Tech Tree, even after the demo has been put out on Steam. For example, now you can see all the benefits of a technology you're about to put your country's brightest scientific minds to:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/6ed9b6ddee30c59f093cba85d09ab75a2efbedd4.jpg[/img]

In other news: we've been improving the AI of the bots for some time now, and they're becoming more witty by day. They're full of surprises: while we were making screenshots for this piece, one of them has reformed Italy into the good ol’ Roman Empire:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44092283/b2649c36ce9b4871b42f2f1c532cca4c61b8a869.jpg[/img]

Perhaps, there's still much work to do to make the bots inherit a more modern political mindframe, but at least they're fun to interact with!

[h2]Next Stop: Steam Next Fest[/h2]

We're very excited for the next week, as we're going to showcase Warnament during the glorious Steam Next! If you're reading this, you probably already hyped about Warnament, but here's a friendly reminder of the best action you can take to support us: add the game to your wishlist!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1201700/Warnament/

You're also so very welcome to join us during our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1201700/view/6027552699436352914]live stream next week[/url]! Just head to the Warnament page on Steam on Tuesday at 9 am PST / 6 pm CET, and say hi or ask any Warnament-related questions.

And please don't restrain yourself from sharing a link to Warnament with your friends! Remember: we've got multiplayer on the way (which is already in testing), so it'd be great to have some Warnament buddies around to divide the world with.

And once the Fest is over, there're new features to be added to the beta. See you next month with more exciting news!
